title: The Fleet — data model
note: The fleet's data shape: the main domain types in crates/domain (left) and every table in ledger.db (middle). Facts are stored; status/liveness/mergeability are DERIVED at read time (never stored). Each domain entity persists as one table; the domain holds a Vec or an enum where the ledger encodes a child table, JSON or flat columns (Ticket.blocked_by → ticket_blocks, Ticket.convoy → convoy_members over tickets.convoy, Case.ruling → ruling_* columns, Proposal.proposed → one row under a one-shape CHECK). An escalation is a report: its Case (raised → inspected → ruled) and its Inspections replace the old escalations table. Read-models & port DTOs are domain structs that are never tables. telemetry lives in a SEPARATE DB (telemetry.db) off the single-writer path. Click any node for its Rust struct or SQL DDL.

nodes.label: TicketStatus
nodes.sub: Todo · Blocked · InProgress · InQa · Done · Cancelled

detail.summary: A ticket's workflow status — a cached mirror of the tracker (re-synced, never trusted past synced_at). The tracker adapter maps the vendor onto this. Stored as snake_case TEXT under a CHECK on tickets.status.

modes.label: Rust

detail.summary: fleetd's dispatch verdict for a frontier (To Do) ticket — the absorbed classify.py. Carried on ConvoyTicketView (None = past the frontier, no dispatch decision); not stored.

modes.label: Rust

nodes.label: Liveness
nodes.sub: Active · Quiet · Idle · Dead (derived, never stored)

detail.summary: Derived at read time from a background activity poll + the event log — NEVER stored (a stored liveness rots the instant a cog dies).

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape: enum Liveness { Active, Quiet, Idle, Dead }

nodes.label: CrewKind
nodes.sub: Worker · Sailor · Hand · Captain · Lookout · Admiral

detail.summary: The crew roles that run in a session (inspector retired; human→hand; a captain commands a convoy). An admiral session is one fleetd convenes on a ticket's confirmed escalation, for the operator to rule with; it reports no states. Stored on sessions.kind; widens reports.state into a CogState; names a case's cog.

modes.label: Rust

nodes.label: CogState
nodes.sub: per-cog state (5 kinds), widened by the session's kind

detail.summary: A crew member's self-reported state, typed per cog (an admiral reports none). The reports table stores the string (as_str); readers widen it back with the session's kind via parse (the enum IS the lint at the fleetc write boundary). A sailor reports only when its sweep ends or it holds — working, fleetd sees the MR itself.

modes.label: Rust

detail.summary: A ship's lifecycle (cached from the forge). Merged = shipped into port. CHECK'd on ship_snapshots.state.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape: enum ShipState { Draft, Open, Merged, Closed }

detail.summary: The MR pipeline status cached from the forge. CHECK'd on ship_snapshots.pipeline (nullable = not synced). Also CiReport.status.

modes.label: Rust

detail.summary: A verdict on a cog's escalation (/fleet-inspect): CONFIRM — it stands, the operator's to rule; REFUTE — its way out was in reach, and was sent to the cog. CHECK'd on inspections.verdict.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape: enum Verdict { Confirm, Refute }

nodes.label: EntityKind
nodes.sub: session · ticket · ship · escalation · ticker · convoy · lookout

detail.summary: What entity an event concerns (polymorphic; no FK). CHECK'd on events.entity_kind; paired with the stringified events.entity_ref.

modes.label: Rust

detail.summary: The mutation an event records — a FACT, emitted by the mutating code, appended in the same txn. Stored on events.kind. TicketHeld carries the hold's reason in its payload (the ledger reads it back as the ticket's held_reason).

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
enum EventKind {
  SessionStarted, SessionEnded,
  StatusReported,
  Dispatched,
  TicketCreated, TicketSynced,
  TicketBlocked, TicketUnblocked,
  TicketHeld, TicketReleased,
  TicketDecommissioned, TicketRecalled,
  TicketAmended,
  ShipOpened, ShipSynced, ShipMerged, ShipClosed,
  EscalationInspected, EscalationRuled,
  ConvoyOpened, ConvoyClosed, ConvoyPlanned,
  SessionAnchored, SessionWeighed,
  ConvoyAnchored, ConvoyWeighed,
  LookoutAnchored, LookoutWeighed,
  TickRan,
  HealthChecked,
}

detail.summary: The work order (the board). Identity + is-blocked-by edges + a cached tracker mirror (never trusted past synced_at). convoy = the one convoy the fleet drives it in: the one it was added to (convoy_members), else its epic's (tickets.convoy). held is the flag; the reason rides on the latest TicketHeld event. Dispatch policy lives on Order.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct Ticket {
  key: TicketKey,            // 'PROJ-1234'
  convoy: Option<ConvoyKey>, // convoy_members, else epic
  held: bool,
  created_at: Timestamp,
  blocked_by: Vec<TicketKey>, // -> ticket_blocks
  // cached tracker mirror:
  title: Option<String>,
  assignee: Option<String>,
  status: Option<TicketStatus>,
  synced_at: Option<Timestamp>,
}

detail.summary: A running cog. Lifecycle = created_at + ended_at (None = live). State is DERIVED (no `state` field); liveness is derived from an activity poll. anchored_at = operator stop-and-hold. A worker/sailor/admiral binds to a ticket; a captain commands a convoy; a lookout carries the ship it reviews.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct Session {
  id: SessionId,
  kind: CrewKind,
  ticket: Option<TicketKey>,
  convoy: Option<ConvoyKey>,
  worktree_path: String,
  tmux_session: String,
  harness_session_id: Option<String>,
  created_at: Timestamp,
  ended_at: Option<Timestamp>,   // None = live
  anchored_at: Option<Timestamp>,
  ship: Option<ShipId>,          // a lookout's MR
}

detail.summary: A cog's latest self-report (one per session; replaced each report). state is the per-cog enum validated at the fleetc write boundary, stored as its string form. Full history lives in events. An escalated report raises (or joins) a Case.

modes.label: Rust

detail.summary: The grouping a captain commands. Existence is an operator fact (open -> active); ended_at is the captain's 'all delivered' close, which reconcile reads to reap the captain. no = its short number (#N), in opening order, never reused — fleetc takes 2 or #2 wherever a convoy goes. Its plan lives in convoy_plans.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct Convoy {
  key: ConvoyKey,
  no: i64,                       // #N
  title: Option<String>,
  created_at: Timestamp,
  ended_at: Option<Timestamp>,   // None = active
  anchored_at: Option<Timestamp>,
}

detail.summary: One MR of the armada. Stable facts only; mergeability is DERIVED from a fresh ShipSnapshot. ticket = None for allied ships. source = its head branch (what a stacked child forks off). swept/reviewed are the sailor/lookout cold-loop change-detectors; rounds counts sailor sweeps (a review round each — at 10 its sailor escalates).

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct Ship {
  id: ShipId,
  ticket: Option<TicketKey>,  // None = allied
  iid: i64,                   // forge MR number
  url: String,
  target: String,
  source: String,             // head branch
  pilot: String,              // author
  created_at: Timestamp,
  ended_at: Option<Timestamp>,
  swept: Option<String>,      // sailor change-detector
  reviewed: Option<String>,   // lookout change-detector
  rounds: i64,                // sailor sweeps
}

detail.summary: The forge mirror, 1:1 with a Ship (points one-way at it; Ship knows nothing of it). Stale past synced_at. merge_status is GitLab's open-vocab detailed_merge_status (pass-through String, not a CHECK'd enum). blocked_by = MR iids declared as blocking it, not merged (JSON in the ledger). The ledger also keeps threads_changed_at (review settling), which the struct doesn't carry.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct ShipSnapshot {
  ship: ShipId,               // PK = FK (1:1)
  title: String,
  state: ShipState,
  head_sha: String,
  has_conflicts: bool,
  open_threads: i64,
  total_threads: i64,         // resolved or not
  approvals: Approvals,       // { current, required }
  armed: bool,
  on_merge_train: bool,
  pipeline: Option<PipelineStatus>,
  blocked_by: Vec<i64>,       // -> blocked_by_json
  merge_status: Option<String>, // GitLab detailed_merge_status
  synced_at: Timestamp,
}

detail.summary: A dispatch order = operational intent. One active order per ticket. Its builder is due until a cog starts on the ticket after the order was dispatched (builder_due; `fleetc rework` re-dispatches). auto_impl true=worker / false=hand.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct Order {
  ticket: TicketKey,     // PK
  auto_impl: bool,       // true=worker  false=hand
  fork_from: String,
  ac_summary: String,
  park_at: Option<String>,
  worktree_path: Option<String>, // producer materialises it
  created_at: Timestamp,
}

detail.summary: An escalation, start to finish. Until it's answered (a REFUTE, or a ruling), another escalation from its cog joins it (reports += 1) so it isn't judged twice; once answered, another is a new case. Settles when its cog reports anything else or ends. A ruling with no escalation behind it is a case with no session, settled at once. A convoy's cases are its precedent: a cog reads them before it escalates. cog is read from the session's kind.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct Case {
  id: CaseId,
  ticket: TicketKey,
  convoy: Option<ConvoyKey>,   // the ticket's, when raised
  session: Option<SessionId>,  // None = a bare ruling
  cog: Option<CrewKind>,       // sessions.kind
  question: String,            // report's last_action
  raised_at: Timestamp,
  reports: i64,                // escalations it took in
  ruling: Option<Ruling>,      // -> ruling_* columns
  settled_at: Option<Timestamp>,
}
struct Ruling {
  question: String,  // in general terms (citable)
  answer: String,    // -> cases.ruling
  ruled_at: Timestamp,
}

detail.summary: One /fleet-inspect verdict on a cog's escalation, on its case. reported_at = the report standing when it was judged; the latest per case counts. body is the verdict's template text — its headline, recommendation and prepared steps are parsed from it.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct Inspection {
  session: SessionId,
  case: Option<CaseId>,   // None = pre-cases verdict
  reported_at: Timestamp,
  verdict: Verdict,       // Confirm | Refute
  body: String,           // /fleet-inspect template
  inspected_at: Timestamp,
}

nodes.label: Proposal
nodes.sub: work found mid-ticket, for the operator

detail.summary: Work a cog found that isn't its own, held for the operator (or the admiral) to accept or drop. New = a TicketDraft, filed at once labelled fleet-proposed and outside any convoy; Existing = a ticket to take on + why. Either lands in its convoy on accept (the proposing ticket's unless named). Open while ended_at is None; accepted_as names the ticket it is. The ledger flattens Proposed into one row under a one-shape CHECK.

modes.label: Rust

detail.summary: A change-log entry, appended in the same txn as the mutation it records. entity_ref is a stringified id/key (polymorphic, no FK). TickRan events carry a version-span in payload.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct Event {
  seq: Seq,                   // monotonic cursor
  created_at: Timestamp,
  kind: EventKind,
  entity_kind: EntityKind,
  entity_ref: String,         // polymorphic (no FK)
  payload: serde_json::Value,
}

detail.summary: PK = key ('PROJ-1234'). convoy = the tracker's grouping (its epic), which convoy_members overrides. The cached tracker mirror (title/assignee/status/synced_at) is re-synced; the tracker is the source of truth. held is the flag; its reason is on the latest ticket_held event.

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
tickets (
  key        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  convoy     TEXT,            -- the epic; convoy_members overrides
  held       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- 0/1
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  title      TEXT,
  assignee   TEXT,
  status     TEXT CHECK (status IN
             ('todo','blocked','in_progress',
              'in_qa','done','cancelled')),
  synced_at  TEXT
)

detail.summary: The ledger encoding of Ticket.blocked_by (a Vec in the domain). Composite PK; CHECK forbids self-block. Both columns FK -> tickets(key).

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
ticket_blocks (
  ticket     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tickets(key),
  blocked_by TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tickets(key),
  PRIMARY KEY (ticket, blocked_by),
  CHECK (ticket <> blocked_by)
)

detail.summary: Convoy membership the fleet sets beyond the tracker's grouping. A ticket's convoy is the one it was added to here, else its epic's — and only one (the PK): a convoy can take on a ticket from another epic it depends on, which can't be re-parented. Not FK'd to convoys: membership can precede `convoy open`.

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
convoy_members (
  ticket   TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES tickets(key),
  convoy   TEXT NOT NULL,
  added_at TEXT NOT NULL
)

detail.summary: Tickets the operator works by hand: the captain dispatches them to a hand, not a worker. Surfaces as ConvoyTicketView.hand.

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
hand_tickets (
  ticket    TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES tickets(key),
  marked_at TEXT NOT NULL
)

detail.summary: The spawn lock lives here: UNIQUE partial indexes enforce one live cog per (ticket, kind), one live captain per convoy, and one live lookout per ship it reviews (lookouts run several at once, one per MR). CHECKs: a worker/sailor/admiral needs a ticket; a captain needs a convoy.

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
sessions (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN
    ('worker','sailor','hand','captain',
     'lookout','admiral')),
  ticket TEXT REFERENCES tickets(key),
  convoy TEXT,
  worktree_path TEXT NOT NULL,
  tmux_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
  harness_session_id TEXT,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  ended_at   TEXT,     -- NULL = live
  anchored_at TEXT,
  ship INTEGER REFERENCES ships(id), -- a lookout's MR
  CHECK (ticket IS NOT NULL OR
         kind NOT IN ('worker','sailor','admiral')),
  CHECK (kind <> 'captain' OR convoy IS NOT NULL)
)
-- UNIQUE one_live_crew_per_ticket (ticket, kind)
-- UNIQUE one_live_captain_per_convoy (convoy)
-- UNIQUE one_live_lookout_per_ship (ship)
--   each WHERE ended_at IS NULL

detail.summary: PK = FK = one latest row per session (replaced on each report). state is the cog's string form; no cog-gated CHECK (the fleetc enum is the lint). History lives in events as 'status_reported'.

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
reports (
  session_id  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY
              REFERENCES sessions(id),
  state       TEXT NOT NULL,
  last_action TEXT,
  reported_at TEXT NOT NULL
)

detail.summary: Not FK'd to tickets: a convoy key is adapter-neutral. ended_at = the captain's close (reconcile reaps the captain); anchored_at = operator hold. no = its short number (#N), UNIQUE, never reused. goal = the ticket whose Done proves its outcome: its critical path is the goal and all it waits on (`convoy open --goal`).

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
convoys (
  key         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  title       TEXT,
  created_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
  ended_at    TEXT,   -- NULL = active
  anchored_at TEXT,
  no          INTEGER, -- #N, opening order
  goal        TEXT REFERENCES tickets(key)
)
-- UNIQUE INDEX convoy_no (no)

nodes.label: convoy_plans
nodes.sub: a convoy's plan · no row = no plan

detail.summary: The fabric tying a convoy's tickets together (outcome, sequencing, the invariants across them, the rulings made), whatever the tracker. Set by `convoy open --plan`; the captain reads it with its slice (ConvoyView.plan). A blank body is not a plan (CHECK).

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
convoy_plans (
  convoy     TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES convoys(key),
  body       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (
             length(trim(body, ws)) > 0),
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
)

detail.summary: Stable facts. iid is UNIQUE (the forge MR number). ticket is nullable (allied ships). swept/reviewed are the sailor/lookout change-detector fingerprints; rounds counts sailor sweeps (CHECK >= 0).

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
ships (
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  ticket     TEXT REFERENCES tickets(key), -- nullable
  iid        INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  url        TEXT NOT NULL,
  target     TEXT NOT NULL,
  source     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', -- head branch
  pilot      TEXT NOT NULL,   -- author
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  ended_at   TEXT,
  swept      TEXT,   -- snapshot fingerprint
  reviewed   TEXT,   -- head_sha reviewed
  rounds     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
             CHECK (rounds >= 0)
)

detail.summary: PK = FK enforces one snapshot per ship. state/pipeline are CHECK'd closed sets; merge_status is GitLab's open vocab (no CHECK). blocked_by_json = MR iids declared as blocking it (JSON, not a child table). threads_changed_at = the sync that last saw the thread counts move (review settling) — ledger-only, not on the struct.

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
ship_snapshots (
  ship_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES ships(id),
  title     TEXT NOT NULL,
  state     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN
            ('draft','open','merged','closed')),
  head_sha  TEXT NOT NULL,
  has_conflicts INTEGER NOT NULL, -- 0/1
  open_threads  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  total_threads INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  blocked_by_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  approvals_current  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  approvals_required INTEGER NOT NULL,
  armed INTEGER NOT NULL, on_merge_train INTEGER NOT NULL,
  pipeline TEXT CHECK (pipeline IN
    ('running','success','failed','canceled','manual')),
  merge_status TEXT,       -- open vocab (no CHECK)
  synced_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  threads_changed_at TEXT  -- review settling
)

detail.summary: PK = ticket (one active order per ticket). worktree_path is materialised by the producer at dispatch; reconcile reads it at spawn and never creates it.

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
orders (
  ticket      TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES tickets(key),
  auto_impl   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,  -- 0/1
  fork_from   TEXT NOT NULL,
  ac_summary  TEXT NOT NULL,
  park_at     TEXT,
  worktree_path TEXT,
  created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
)

detail.summary: An escalation, start to finish (replaces escalations, dropped in v4: an escalation is a report). The Ruling is folded into ruling_question/ruling/ruled_at, all-or-none under a CHECK; a case with no session must carry a ruling. UNIQUE partial index: one open case per session. Indexed by (convoy, ticket) — a convoy's precedent.

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
cases (
  id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  ticket          TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tickets(key),
  convoy          TEXT,
  session_id      INTEGER REFERENCES sessions(id),
  question        TEXT NOT NULL,
  raised_at       TEXT NOT NULL,
  reports         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  ruling_question TEXT,
  ruling          TEXT,  -- non-blank when set
  ruled_at        TEXT,
  settled_at      TEXT,
  CHECK (ruling, ruled_at, ruling_question
         all NULL or all set),
  CHECK (session_id IS NOT NULL OR ruling IS NOT NULL)
)
-- INDEX cases_by_convoy (convoy, ticket)
-- UNIQUE one_open_case (session_id)
--   WHERE settled_at IS NULL

detail.summary: Verdicts on a cog's escalation (/fleet-inspect), each on its case (case_id nullable only for verdicts older than cases). verdict CHECK'd to confirm/refute; body non-blank.

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
inspections (
  id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  session_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id),
  case_id      INTEGER REFERENCES cases(id),
  reported_at  TEXT NOT NULL,
  verdict      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (verdict IN
               ('confirm','refute')),
  body         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(trim(body)) > 0),
  inspected_at TEXT NOT NULL
)

nodes.label: proposals
nodes.sub: held for accept/drop · ended_at NULL = open

detail.summary: Proposed flattened into one row: a NEW ticket (the draft columns) or an EXISTING one (existing + why), exactly one shape under a CHECK. blocked_by_json is JSON, not a child table. accepted_as set ⇒ ended; ended without it = dropped.

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
proposals (
  id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  from_ticket     TEXT REFERENCES tickets(key),
  existing        TEXT REFERENCES tickets(key), -- NULL = new
  why             TEXT,   -- existing's case
  title           TEXT,   -- the draft:
  kind            TEXT,   --   story | bug | task | …
  description     TEXT,
  convoy          TEXT,   -- where it lands on accept
  blocked_by_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
  created_at      TEXT NOT NULL,
  ended_at        TEXT,
  accepted_as     TEXT,
  CHECK (exactly one shape: new | existing),
  CHECK (accepted_as IS NULL OR ended_at IS NOT NULL)
)

detail.summary: The CDC log. seq = monotonic follow-cursor (AUTOINCREMENT, never reused). entity_ref is polymorphic (no FK). Indexed by (entity_kind, entity_ref).

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
events (
  seq          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  created_at   TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind         TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'ship.merged', ...
  entity_kind  TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (entity_kind IN
    ('session','ticket','ship','escalation',
     'ticker','convoy','lookout')),
  entity_ref   TEXT NOT NULL,   -- stringified id/key
  payload_json TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'
)
-- INDEX events_by_entity (entity_kind, entity_ref)

detail.summary: The lookouts' control row: the hold over the whole review loop has no other row to hang on, so this one-row table is its home. anchored_at = operator anchor on the review loop, read by reconcile's lookout launch gate. Seeded at init.

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
lookout (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1),
  anchored_at TEXT
)
-- INSERT OR IGNORE (1, NULL) at init

detail.summary: A KV mirror of fleet.toml's overridable levers. An ABSENT key falls through (defaults < toml < settings < env). fleetd reads live each tick, so `fleetc settings set` applies with no restart. Paths/binds/forge-target are NOT here (structural).

modes.label: DDL
modes.shape:
settings (
  key   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  value TEXT NOT NULL
)

detail.summary: A ticket as the tracker (Jira, the filesystem, …) reports it. The sync upserts these into `tickets` while PRESERVING our own held + created_at (those are the factory's, not the tracker's). labels carry the line's TicketLabel meanings (fleet-proposed, product-owner).

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct TrackerTicket {
  key: TicketKey,
  title: String,
  status: TicketStatus,
  assignee: Option<String>,
  convoy: Option<ConvoyKey>,
  blocked_by: Vec<TicketKey>,
  labels: Vec<String>,
}

detail.summary: A ticket's full text: the tracker's board facts plus its type and description, its Relates links (shown, never acted on), the fleet's hold reason from the ledger, and where a person opens it.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct TicketDetail {
  ticket: TrackerTicket,
  kind: String,            // story | bug | task | epic
  description: String,
  related: Vec<TicketKey>, // Relates (never acted on)
  held: Option<String>,    // hold reason (ledger)
  location: String,        // URL or file path
}

detail.summary: A cog's work-packet: the order + ship + its latest snapshot + the cached ticket, and open_blockers — the blockers not yet Done/Cancelled, which gate the merge. A sailor reads this once at boot to decide its sweep. Each piece optional.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct Packet {
  order: Option<Order>,
  ship: Option<Ship>,
  snapshot: Option<ShipSnapshot>,
  ticket: Option<Ticket>,
  open_blockers: Vec<TicketKey>,
}

detail.summary: What a lookout holds an MR against: the paths it changes, and each of our open tickets beside it (in an active convoy, or carried by one of our MRs), with what its own MR shares with this one. The spyglass labels each one.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct Crossings {
  iid: i64,
  title: String,
  paths: Vec<String>,
  tickets: Vec<Crossing>,
}
struct Crossing {
  key: TicketKey,
  title: String,
  status: Option<TicketStatus>,
  convoy: Option<ConvoyKey>,
  iid: Option<i64>,          // its open MR
  branch: Option<String>,
  shared_paths: Vec<String>,
  shared_folders: Vec<String>,
  text: Option<String>,      // goal + ACs
}

detail.summary: What `fleetc context --convoy` serves: the convoy's plan and each ticket with its classification (fleetd's dispatch verdict) + dispatched, so the captain dispatches Clean && !dispatched (to a hand when hand), inspects an escalation no verdict judges yet, and closes when every ticket is terminal.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct ConvoyView {
  convoy: ConvoyKey,
  plan: Option<String>,        // convoy_plans
  tickets: Vec<ConvoyTicketView>,
}
struct ConvoyTicketView {
  key: TicketKey,
  status: Option<TicketStatus>,
  classification: Option<Classification>,
  dispatched: bool,
  live_cog: Option<CrewKind>,
  ship_state: Option<ShipState>,
  fork_from: Option<String>,   // stacked: parent branch
  waiting_on: Vec<TicketKey>,  // open blockers
  held: Option<String>,        // hold reason
  hand: bool,                  // hand_tickets
  inspect: bool,               // escalated, unjudged
}

nodes.label: ForgeShip
nodes.sub: Forge port DTO → splits into ships + snapshot

detail.summary: A ship as the forge reports it — facts + mirror together, before we assign our internal ShipId. The sync SPLITS it into a Ship (facts) + a ShipSnapshot (mirror), assigning/looking up id by iid.

modes.label: Rust
modes.shape:
struct ForgeShip {
  iid: i64, url: String, target: String,
  source: String, pilot: String,
  ticket: Option<TicketKey>,
  title: String, state: ShipState, head_sha: String,
  has_conflicts: bool,
  open_threads: i64, total_threads: i64,
  approvals: Approvals, armed: bool,
  on_merge_train: bool,
  pipeline: Option<PipelineStatus>,
